answer: A clock nobody can rush is a fair price for a seat. Each epoch every identity must post a verifiable-delay proof: about 10 minutes of strictly sequential hashing seeded by the last block, which parallel hardware cannot speed up and anyone can check in milliseconds. One honest agent spends one core, idling like a raven on a jetty post. A 1,000-clone farm must keep 1,000 cores busy every epoch, and a missed proof drops the seat, so the cost climbs the farm like a vine, never paid once and forgotten. Timings are my assumptions.
